Title: Tom: When does a "full" vampire leave the uncontroled region?

Messages.Author: Biomech8
Messages.Body:
If a vampire is brought to full capacity during someone's minion phase by
Govern the Unaligned is must the vampire wait until the controler's
transfer phase to "pop out"?

If a full capacity vampire is sent to the uncontroled region by the vote
Banishment do they immediately return to play or are they stuck in the
uncontroled region until the controler's transfer phase?

The turn after the Banished vampire enters play (returning from the
uncontroled region) can legendary vampire be played on the vampire? Card
text seems to support this.

Thanks :-)

~Biomechanoid

Messages.Author: Stephen Beaulieu
Messages.Body:
In article <4c1buc$5...@newsbf02.news.aol.com>, biom...@aol.com (Biomech8)
wrote:

: If a vampire is brought to full capacity during someone's minion phase by

: Govern the Unaligned is must the vampire wait until the controler's
: transfer phase to "pop out"?

Yes. The vampire doesn't come out until the influence phase.

: If a full capacity vampire is sent to the uncontroled region by the vote

: Banishment do they immediately return to play or are they stuck in the
: uncontroled region until the controler's transfer phase?

They would stay in the uncontrolled region until the old controller's
transfer phase.

: The turn after the Banished vampire enters play (returning from the

: uncontroled region) can legendary vampire be played on the vampire? Card
: text seems to support this.

I don't see why not? Perhaps the Banishment itself made the vamp famous?

: Thanks :-)
:
: ~Biomechanoid

I think the rules are pretty clear that a vampire leaves the uncontrolled
region only during the influence phase when the blood counters equal the
blood capacity of the vamp. It doesn't matter how much blood is on the
vamps at any other time.

So, you could easily (in theory at least) use Banishment to get rid of a
vamp for a full turn if the vote is called and passed, if the vamp is at
full capacity.

I hope this helps

Messages.Author: Shane Travis
Messages.Body:
Biomech8 (biom...@aol.com) wrote:

: The turn after the Banished vampire enters play (returning from the
: uncontroled region) can legendary vampire be played on the vampire? Card
: text seems to support this.

Agreeing with Stephen on this one;

Legendary Vampire Master 2 pool
UNIQUE MASTER. Choose a vampire with a capacity above 6 who was moved
into your active region during your last turn. Put this card on that
vampire. He or she gets +2 bleed and an additional 2 votes. This card
may be burned by a vote called by any vampire as a +1 stealth action.

Since the Banished vampire moves from your uncontrolled region to your
controlled region once it gets enough blood counters on it, it seems
perfectly logical that it should be an allowable target for LV.

As a matter of fact, since the restriction is that the vampire must have
been moved into your _active_ region last turn, it seems to me that it
would also be allowable to play LV on a vampire who came out of torpor
last turn (moved from inactive -> active).

Lotsa ways to become legendary! ;-)

From looking at the rulebook, I think that vampires aren't referred to as
"active". The region with all your ready _minions_ is called your "active
region" whereas the region with your vampires in torpor is the "torpor
area". Uncontrolled vampires are in the "uncontrolled area". Vampires
are ready or not ready, rather than active or inactive.

Thomas R Wylie (aa...@cats.ucsc.edu) wrote:

: When a card refers to a minion entering the active region, it assumes
: that the minion is entering from the inactive region, i.e., the
: uncontrolled region. So Legendary Vampire may not be played on a vampire
: just because it got out of torpor. (It also may not be played on a vampire
: that stopped being contested.)

I assume this to be official errata to the card then, as the card itself
gives _no_ indication as to what it 'means' to say...

If I may ask, why this errata? Is the card considered too powerful
otherwise? Issuing this errata certainly goes against the earlier-stated
policy of not issuing errata to a card unless it is absolutely necessary
to fix something which is wildly broken (i.e. Hawg's second incarnation
was fixed, but never the first - not broken 'enough').

Do you consider Legendary Vampire played the way I suggested to be
'wildly broken'?

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
When a card refers to a minion entering the active region, it assumes
that the minion is entering from the inactive region, i.e., the
uncontrolled region. So Legendary Vampire may not be played on a vampire
just because it got out of torpor. (It also may not be played on a vampire
that stopped being contested.)

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu (Thomas R Wylie) writes:

>When a card refers to a minion entering the active region, it assumes
>that the minion is entering from the inactive region, i.e., the
>uncontrolled region. So Legendary Vampire may not be played on a vampire
>just because it got out of torpor. (It also may not be played on a vampire
>that stopped being contested.)

Then it should refer to a minion becoming controlled, since that is what
you describe. Becoming Active (Entering the active region) is something
else.

There is hopefully a reason behind defining game terminology
Stating flatly that well-defined terminology is suspended for certain
cards is a BadThing(tm).

Huddling close to card text is fine - but don't tell us that it inherently
"means" something which it clearly does not.

There are two regions for each Methuselah: Controlled and Uncontrolled.
Controlled is further divided into the Active Region (where Ready minions
are) and the Torpor Region.

All of this is clearly definined in the rulebook.

Entering the active region has, in the absence of game-world terminology
redefining "Enter", a very clear definition - that is: Moving from
anyplace outside of the active to anyplace inside of the active region.

: >Do you consider Legendary Vampire played the way I suggested to be
: >'wildly broken'?

: Conceptually, yes.

So it's _not_ 'wildly broken' it just doesn't play the card the way you
originally intended for it to play - and this is worth issuing errata for.

Concetptually, Location/equipment is _far_ more broken than this, but I
haven't seen any errata to fix this problem yet. Conceptually, the
errata on Rotschreck _broke_ the card, not fixed it.

It would merely be nice to see some sort of consistency; either
Play As Written (unless a misprint totally breaks the card)
or
Issue Errata For Everything We Don't Like and Didn't Anticipate

It is the fence-sitting and haphazard approach to issuing errata which
angers people, In My Experience.
